channel.description: Signal & Noise is a personal podcast made for Augusto Restrepo. Each episode takes a topic he's been following — articles, posts, research and conversations he curates from across the web — and double-clicks on it. Max, the optimist, makes the bull case; Lena, the skeptic, pokes holes in it. Together they separate the signal from the noise, so the big ideas are easier to understand and judge. Casual, curious, and grounded in facts.

item.title: Loud Rumors, Thin Receipts
item.description:
Thesis Check special: New Rails (first coverage; news window ~Oct 12–Nov 13, 2026, weighted to the Oct 29 Binance hack onward). Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) start with a deep look at this week's crypto flush and the Binance rumors. Then they cover Robinhood's October numbers, Nu's record Q3 and the four tokens (Solana, XRP, Jito, Hyperliquid), checked against the DRAFT New Rails framework from Nov 3.
Binance, verified: Oct 29 hot-wallet hack, about $6.3B (Binance; Chainalysis ~$5.9B, TRM ~$6.4B); FBI attribution to North Korea's TraderTraitor (Oct 31); DOJ (Nov 12): more than $2.7B frozen and more than $1.2B court-authorized for seizure or restraint; ~56-hour withdrawal halt; ~$3.6B net outflow in the first 9.5 hours after reopening (Binance-reported); spot share ~48% to ~42% (Kaiko via Bloomberg); coverage declared complete Nov 12 from company funds; new proof-of-reserves snapshot (BTC 100.05%, ETH 100.02%, USDT 104.34%, self-reported). Binance, unverified: that Binance is pushing prices into liquidation clusters to cover losses (a theory aired on Simply Bitcoin Live, which itself called it speculation); that tens of thousands of accounts are frozen for liquidity (Binance's Yi He says the freezes are law-enforcement orders); and 1:1 backing until the zero-knowledge proof (due ~Nov 14) is published. We found no on-chain evidence, regulator action or credible reporting supporting manipulation or insolvency.
Nu Q3'26 (Nov 12): record net income $1.09B (+31% FXN), ROE 32%; gross revenue $6.3B (+37%); customers 143M (+~13% y/y); ARPAC ~$18 (+21%); deposits $47.5B (+19%); 15–90 NPL 4.9%, 90+ NPL 7.3%; efficiency guide lowered to 19–19.5%. EPS roughly in line (sources differ). Stock about +11% on Nov 13. Robinhood October data (Nov 12): funded customers 28.9M (+7%); net deposits $15.1B (46% annualized, includes ~$6B Dell Trump Accounts gift); crypto volume $17.0B (−48% y/y); event contracts +136%.
Suggestions only (draft framework, nothing scored): C1★ rails growth YELLOW (blended customer growth ~10–12%; on-chain legs above floors on Q3 data); C2 money onto rails YELLOW, provisional (stablecoins down QTD on Solana ~−7% and XRPL ~−25%); C3 monetization leaning GREEN but incomplete (SOL/HYPE fees y/y not pulled). Add an exchange-trust (proof-of-reserves) watch item; decide HYPE OI vs volume share for C1★. Buy rules v3: New Rails is a label, so it has no v3 action; under the crypto hard floor SOL, XRP and JTO are below their 200-day averages (wait), and HYPE is the only one above. Biggest risk: money leaving the rails (stablecoin supply shrinking, crypto volumes down by half, Fed hike odds rising); for Nu, Brazil macro and credit. Dates: ~Nov 14 Binance ZK proof · Nov 17 Nvidia (tentative) · Dec 3 SOL/XRP sizing decision · Dec 8–9 FOMC · mid-Dec HOOD November data · Dec 31 Q4 end · Jan 18, 2027 GENIUS effective · Feb 9, 2027 HOOD Q4 (tentative) · Feb 24, 2027 NU Q4 (tentative).
Chapters: 1. Loud rumors, thin receipts; 2. The double click: what actually happened at Binance; 3. The rumors: manipulation and frozen accounts; 4. Call-in: Declan, who used to guard the hot wallets; 5. Robinhood: crypto halves, deposits don't; 6. Nu: a record quarter in a Brazilian storm; 7. Call-in: Camila on Brazilian credit; 8. The crypto four: Solana, XRP, Jito, Hyperliquid; 9. Verdict: lights, biggest risk, dates.
Sources: Nu Q3 2026 release, 6-K financial statements and earnings presentation (Nov 12), Investing.com call transcript; Robinhood October 2026 operating data (Nov 12) and Q3 2026 release; US DOJ press release (Nov 12); Binance statements via Bitcoin Magazine, crypto.news, Unchained, TokenPost, Reuters/US News (Nov 3) and Cryptopolitan; CoinLive/BigTime research (Kaiko, Bloomberg, Chainalysis, TRM data); Simply Bitcoin (Nov 12); CoinDesk, The Block, Decrypt, FXStreet (Nov 13 markets); Benzinga (Nov 5); Stocktwits/Yahoo and Investing.com (Oct 26 Brazil selloff); CryptoPotato/SoSoValue and TokenPost (ETF flows); DefiLlama (stablecoins); CoinGecko (prices, 200-day averages); BAMservatory (Jito BAM); FXStreet on Hyperliquid's Q3 report; ICE investor relations; Raoul Pal live show (Nov 2); Robinhood market data (quotes, earnings dates).
Caveats: Declan and Camila are fictional call-in guests, and their comments are illustrative. The 10am.pro WhatsApp group was not read because the Mac was offline. Some token metrics are second-hand or Q3-only, as marked in the framework. This is not investment advice.

item.title: Beat, Raise, Sold Anyway
item.description:
Thesis Check: Electricity (first coverage; news window ~Oct 12–Nov 10, 2026, weighted to the last two weeks). Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go through three earnings reports and a rough month for AI-power stocks: GE Vernova (Oct 28: orders +96% organic, backlog ~$197B, guide raised, ≥130 GW gas target, $9B Trench deal; today's SoftBank write-down), Constellation (Nov 9: adj. EPS $5.06 vs $3.04, FY guide raised to $12.50–$12.80, Google and Amazon PPAs, $5B conditional DOE loan, Crane restart now H2 2027) and Cameco (Oct 30: EPS miss on the Key Lake outage, Westinghouse adj. EBITDA +15% y/y, outlook reiterated, AP1000 US deal still unsigned), plus the grid ETF health check. Price path since Oct 9 close: GE Vernova about −21%, Cameco −17%, grid ETF −12%, Constellation −10%, Nasdaq-100 fund −10%; catalysts were the Oct 14 inflation print, Meta's Oct 22 capex/financing news, the Nov 4 midterm result, the Nov 5 Nasdaq drop and today's hot CPI.
Verdict: thesis green, tape red. Suggestions only, nothing changed in the tracker: Cameco C2 (Westinghouse EBITDA trend) yellow to green with footnotes (Cameco overall stays yellow); GE Vernova, Constellation and the grid ETF stay green on all three; add GE Vernova slot conversions as a written watch item; fill the missing Q4 2025 MW figure for Constellation C2; define the Cameco AP1000 slip test (unsigned at the Feb 12 report = about one quarter late, yellow; later = red). Buy rules v3: GE Vernova, Constellation and the grid ETF are add-worthy but closed below their 200-day average (re-check); Cameco is no new money.
Chapters: 1. Beat, raise, sold anyway; 2. GE Vernova: a record quarter and a falling stock; 3. Call-in: Darlene, who actually builds gas plants; 4. GE Vernova's lights, and the canary; 5. Constellation: the one the market believed; 6. Cameco: the miss that wasn't about Westinghouse; 7. Call-in: Hamish, who used to buy the uranium; 8. Cameco's lights, and the grid fund health check; 9. Verdict: thesis green, tape red.
Sources: GE Vernova Q3 2026 press release (SEC EX-99, Oct 28) and 10-Q; Benzinga, BNP Paribas (via Investing.com/Yahoo), The Fly (via Stocktwits/Yahoo) analyst coverage; Constellation Q3 2026 release (Nov 9) and Motley Fool call transcript; Cameco Q3 2026 release, MD&A and call transcript (Oct 30), Cameco DOE release (Jun 23); First Trust GRID fund page (data as of Nov 9); Reuters (via StreetInsider/Investing), CNBC, 24/7 Wall St, Motley Fool and Yahoo/TIKR market coverage; CNBC Investing Club on SoftBank/GE Vernova (Nov 10); Tom Nash YouTube (Oct 19, via TubeRank transcript); Robinhood quotes, daily bars, ratings and earnings dates (read-only, Nov 10 close). Caveats: Cameco pace math uses an estimated CAD/USD rate; Constellation's prior-two-quarter MW comparison is missing Q4 2025; PJM backstop and FERC co-location timing come from a secondary source; no clear catalyst found for GE Vernova's Nov 3 gain; Musk's SoftBank post is as reported by CNBC. The 10am.pro group was not read this time (Mac offline).
Darlene and Hamish are fictional characters; their comments are illustrative and grounded in the episode's sources. This is not investment advice.

item.title: Growth Up, Subscribers Down, Two Reds
item.description:
Thesis Check: Biology is Code, recorded the evening of Hims & Hers' Q3 2026 report (Nov 9, 2026). Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go through the Hims quarter and call: revenue up 49% to about $890M, subscribers down about 100,000 from last quarter, gross margin 57% (74% a year ago), a $33M net loss, a lower full-year revenue midpoint and a second cut to the adjusted EBITDA guide, plus the stock's ~12% drop before the report. They walk each Hims stop-light, then revisit Nautilus two weeks after its Oct 27 report through the thesis's learning goals (milestones, raise terms, how it trades), draft candidate thresholds for its unscored conditions, and close with a verdict and dates to watch.
Suggestions only, nothing changed in the tracker: Hims C1 star green to yellow (and define whether a lower guide midpoint counts as a cut; if so it is red and the keep/sell memo is due by ~Nov 16); C2 green to red (subscribers down q/q); C3 stays red; overall green to red under the standard rule. Nautilus stays unscored; write thresholds before the Jan 15, 2027 review.
Chapters: 1. Hims reported two hours ago, and the screen is red; 2. The Hims quarter: growth up, everything else down; 3. Call-in: Wade on the missing hundred thousand; 4. Hims stop-lights: one star in doubt, two reds; 5. Nautilus, two weeks later: what the experiment has taught us; 6. Call-in: Delia, who has actually bought these machines; 7. Drafting Nautilus's lights before January; 8. Verdict: the thesis is alive, the core name is on probation.
Sources: Hims & Hers Q3 2026 press release (Nov 9, 2026) and Benzinga's transcript of the 5 PM ET call (quotes verbatim from it); Yahoo Finance/Stocktwits, 24/7 Wall St and Benzinga market coverage (Nov 9); Robinhood quotes, daily bars and analyst ratings (read-only, as of ~7:15 PM ET Nov 9; ratings last updated Oct 30); Antonio Linares (@alc2022) posts on X, Nov 6-9 (quoted or paraphrased as marked); Nautilus Q3 2026 press release, call transcript and SEEDS release (Oct 27), Sep 11, 2026 8-K; Augusto's Biology is Code thesis file, scorecard definitions and tracker. Gross-profit dollar comparison is the hosts' own rough math. The Street's Q4 estimate comes from one live blog. The 10am.pro group was not read this time (Mac offline).
Wade and Delia are fictional characters; their comments are illustrative and grounded in the episode's sources. This is not investment advice.

item.title: Texas Turns Blue and the AI Trade Splits
item.description:
An unofficial recap of the past week of the All-In podcast (Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks and David Friedberg), Oct 31 – Nov 7, 2026. Only one new All-In release landed in that window: the election night livestream, "All-In Podcast REACTS to Democrat Sweep!" (also listed as "2026 Election Night Livestream with the Besties!"), streamed live on YouTube on Tuesday, Nov 3, 2026, from about 8:02 to 10:05 PM ET. Jason, Chamath and Friedberg hosted; Sacks was absent. Guests: Sen. Ted Cruz, Rahm Emanuel, Polymarket founder Shane Coplan, Tim Dillon, Taylor Lorenz, Brad Gerstner and Ben Shapiro. The regular weekly episode had not been released when this recap was made. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go topic by topic.
Topics: three things that matter this week; the blue wave as Polymarket and the panel saw it live, and the results since; the Texas governor flip and Chamath's case that data center politics is the main risk to the AI trade; Brad Gerstner's gigawatt and GDP math, the Anthropic IPO question, and Wednesday's split market reaction (neoclouds down, hyperscalers up); Ted Cruz on early-vote math, gridlock and the coalition cracks (farmers, suburbs, Hispanic voters) plus Friedberg on the farm economy; Rahm Emanuel's ethics-and-health-care playbook and the "scorched earth vs. reward the swing voter" debate; Shane Coplan on manipulation and the Brazil miss; Tim Dillon and Taylor Lorenz on cost of living, free speech and taxing wealth; California's Prop 40 billionaire tax; Ben Shapiro's autopsy; a 2028 draft board; and Chamath's "W-2 wages, not GDP" mea culpa.
Made-up call-in: Ruby, a fictional Texas data-center permitting consultant. She is invented for this episode and speaks for no real person or firm; her points are drawn from the public reporting listed below.
Sources: the public Podspun transcript of the livestream (no speaker labels; attributions inferred from context, and where unclear we say "one of them"); YouTube listing for title and stream times; results and market coverage from AP, Ballotpedia, the Texas Secretary of State, Texas Tribune, NBC 5 DFW, the LA Times, ABC7 San Francisco, CNBC, Benzinga (citing Wells Fargo), Business Insider (citing UBS and an NBC exit poll) and MarketWatch. Prop 40 and some House races were still being counted as of Nov 6–7. Numbers are rounded and are the speakers' claims unless flagged as checked. Hosts don't imitate the besties' or guests' voices. Not affiliated with All-In; not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. Three things that matter this week; 2. A blue tsunami in real time; 3. Texas flips, and the data center trade; 4. Call-in: Ruby, a made-up Texas permitting consultant; 5. The Anthropic IPO and the GDP math; 6. Ted Cruz: early warnings and gridlock; 7. Farmers, diesel and the coalition cracks; 8. Rahm Emanuel's playbook: ethics and health care; 9. Scorched earth, or reward the swing voter?; 10. Polymarket on the stand; 11. Tim Dillon, Taylor Lorenz and the vibes; 12. Prop 40 and the billionaire tax; 13. Ben Shapiro's autopsy; 14. The 2028 draft board; 15. Mea culpas, and what to watch.

item.description:
Thesis Check: Apple (AAPL). This is the first full Apple episode, recorded hours after Apple's fiscal Q4 2026 report (Nov 2, after the close). The thesis is checked against the stop-light framework in the tracker. News window: Oct 5 to Nov 2, 2026. Max (bull) vs Lena (skeptic).
Chapters: - Apple reported tonight, and the stock blinked - The numbers: a record September, carried by iPhone and Mac - The guide and the after-hours dip - C-one star: a new category, or just more phone? - Call-in: Russ on why glasses are hard (Russ) - C-two: builder or customer? The Siri question - C-three and the App Store: is the phone becoming optional? - Verdict, biggest risk and dates to watch
Results: revenue $114.5B, up 12% (vs ~$113.4B expected). EPS $2.10, up 14% (vs ~$1.99), including about $0.05 of tariff refunds. iPhone $57.6B, up 17.5%. Mac $10.8B, up 24%. iPad $6.2B, down 10%. Wearables/Home $8.3B, down 8%. Services $31.6B, up about 10% (the slowest since 2022). Gross margin 47.9%, with about 1 point from tariff refunds. Greater China up 21%. December-quarter guide: revenue up 7–10% (Street ~6%), Services up 8–9% (Street ~10%), gross margin 45–46% (below the Street, because of memory and Siri AI inference costs). Stock: closed at $338.32 (−1.8%), then traded around $329 after hours (about −2.6%). Since Sep 30 it is up ~1.6%, while QQQ is down ~8%.
Suggested light changes (suggestions only; the tracker is unchanged): - C1★, a new mainstream category: RED, no change. HomeView is a home hub and the Duo is an iPhone. Glasses (N50) are reported for late 2027 and could slip to 2028. - C2, a seat at the AI table: YELLOW, no change. Apple's own foundation models are trained with Google Gemini technology, and the top model runs in Google Cloud. Siri AI is still beta, with a waitlist and limits, and is not available in the EU or China. - C3, the phone becoming optional: YELLOW, no change. Every Meta, Google/Samsung and OpenAI device is still tethered to the phone or not yet shipping. - Overall: RED / REVISIT (one red; the starred condition is red).
Health verdict: the business is strong and the thesis is unchanged. Apple is harvesting the current platform very well but shows no new category, and it rents part of its AI stack. Biggest risk: Apple's glasses slip again while Meta and Google put their assistants on people's faces. Near term, there is valuation risk (>35x forward) as memory and AI costs squeeze margins.

item.title: Nautilus Q3: Foundation Year, Raise Pending
item.description:
Nautilus Biotechnology (NAUT) reported Q3 2026 results on October 27. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go through the numbers, the Voyager launch timeline, and the analyst Q&A: who asked what, what management committed to, and what it dodged.
In this episode: - Q3: revenue $234K (grant $208K + service $26K), net loss $15.6M ($0.12/share), cash and investments $114.3M, runway guided into Q1 2028 - Roadmap: first beta instrument this year, AKT1 Early Access late 2026, pre-orders early 2027, instrument shipments mid-2027 - Oncology assays (AKT1, EGFR, P53) matching tau-level reproducibility after about a year of development - Q&A with Guggenheim, TD Cowen, Roth Capital and a fourth analyst: customer counts not disclosed, instrument price not final, "27 is a year where we set the foundation and 28 is a year where we really go and scale the business" - Not asked by any analyst: the planned capital raise before mid-2027, and Early Access pricing and margins - Call-ins on instrument buying and on financing
Sources: Nautilus press release (Oct 27, 2026), Benzinga call transcript, Form 8-K (Sep 11, 2026), Investing.com, market quotes as of about 10 AM ET. Management quotes are verbatim from the transcript. Social posts are paraphrased.
Callers Ruth and Kit are fictional characters, and their comments are illustrative. This is not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. Beat, dip, rip; 2. The numbers; 3. The roadmap; 4. The Q&A; 5. Call-ins: the lab and the money; 6. The tape and the chatter; 7. Verdict.

item.title: Tech Digest: The iPhone Duo's Split Verdict, Launch-Day Cracks & a Touch Mac Wednesday — Sam & Nora
item.description:
Sam and Nora on Apple's iPhone Duo launch week. Reviewers are split: Gruber calls the outer phone "a miserable fat little thing" and the inner screen "a splendid, joyful, beautiful tablet." The Verge gave it a 7 and then argued about that score on the Vergecast. Marques Brownlee calls it "first generation fun," and Joanna Stern's robot Hingey folded it 32,640 times. Plus inner-screen cracks along the hinge on launch day, the pre-order mess Gurman calls a mistake, and stock that won't come until January.
Quick hits: Apple's "Pro and Tell" event on Oct 28 (touchscreen MacBook Pro expected), Gurman's Nov 6 retail reset, a HomeView with a robotic arm, Claude Duet, the Downloads-folder AI agent attack, the PHP flaw, Tesla's Model 3 update and the Roadster, and Birdbuddy. Mashable joins the source list this week.
Sequoia angle: Duo trade-ins will come in slowly through the winter, refurb Pros are an easy pitch against a $2,000 phone, and grading used Duos will need a close look at the hinge and inner screen.
Call-in guests Fintan and Marisol share views based only on reported facts.
Sources: The Vergecast, Joanna Stern (The New Things), MKBHD/Waveform, Mark Gurman (Bloomberg Power On, paywalled; re-reports), Daring Fireball, Mashable.

item.description:
An unofficial recap of the past week of the All-In podcast (Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks and David Friedberg), Oct 17–24, 2026. It covers all three All-In releases since last week's recap: the main show, episode 294, "AI Cyber Panic, Ken Griffin's Bubble Warning, The Fall of France?" (released Oct 23, 7:08 PM ET), and two interviews: Figma CEO Dylan Field (Oct 19, 4:43 PM ET) and IBM's Arvind Krishna with Palo Alto Networks' Nikesh Arora (Oct 21, 7:42 PM ET). Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go topic by topic.
Topics: Ken Griffin's bubble warning and Chamath's "negative free cash flow" AI spend argument, the Ramp spend data and the early-AWS analogy; open-weight versus frontier models, explainability and resilient inference; the PHP vulnerability scare (only CVE IDs leaked, per the PHP Foundation) and what defenders should do; agents, banks and who carries liability, including "abliterated" models; tech debt, security budgets, Mythos, Arvind's three war lessons and pooled vulnerability sharing; the quantum clock; Dylan Field on whether AI is killing SaaS, vertical integration, Figma's growth, the "AI psychosis moment" and the OpenAI math result; data-center bans and labor versus capital; France's riots, the 10-year above 5% and the spread versus Germany; the fixes, a SpaceX share for every kid, and the minimum wage fight.

item.title: Biology Eats the Market — Max vs Lena (Special)
item.description:
A one-off special. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) debate Antonio Linares's "bio/acc basket": his claim that biology drives most market returns over the next decade, and his four picks. Nautilus (NAUT) reads the proteome, Recursion (RXRX) designs drugs with A.I., ImmunityBio (IBRX) reboots the immune system with Anktiva, and MiNK Therapeutics (INKT) takes iNKT cell therapy after solid tumors. Max makes the case from the post and its 33-minute video: biology becomes code, a read, design, reboot and strike stack, disciplined management teams, and pharma money already flowing into Recursion. Lena pushes back with the latest filings: Nautilus's first revenue of about $0.2M and its Broadscale delay, Recursion's cash burn, ImmunityBio's 45x sales valuation and the FDA warning letter, and MiNK's roughly $9M cash plus a 17-patient phase 2 with zero responses. A made-up guest, Nigel, drops by to heckle the whole idea of "platform" biotech.

item.title: HIMS Isn't Telemedicine — Max vs Lena (Special)
item.description:
A one-off special. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) talk through "HIMS No Es Telemedicina", a Substack piece by Hernán Jaramillo and Antonio Linares of 10ampro. The piece argues that the market prices HIMS like a call center that hands out prescriptions, and that this is a category error. Its case rests on Linares's "closed loop" idea, with Spotify and Duolingo as comparisons: intake, treatment, follow-up and outcome, all owned by one company. Lena pushes back on the customer-service horror story, the FTC case (including the health-data sharing allegations the article leaves out), acquired versus organic growth, competition from Novo, Amazon and OpenAI, and the empty "sold with margin" box: negative free cash flow and a shrinking gross margin.
Source article (credit): Hernán Jaramillo & Antonio Linares, "HIMS No Es Telemedicina", 10ampro on Substack, Sep 27, 2026, https://substack.com/home/post/p-217692613. The framework comes from Antonio Linares's "The State of the Ontology Velocity" (Sep 15, 2026). Also referenced: the Hims & Hers Q2 2026 results and earnings call (Aug 10, 2026), the FTC complaint and press release (Jul 29, 2026), Teladoc's Q2 2026 results, and public HIMS price data as of the Sep 25, 2026 close. Numbers are rounded. Claims the hosts couldn't verify are flagged on air. This is not investment advice.
